title: Timeline Glitch
blurb: History's calendar is glitching. Three of these really line up. One is pure cap.

cards.say: Cleopatra [lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid], [was born about 250 years after Alexander the Great died], [ruled Egypt as queen for more than 40 years before Rome took over], and [was living in Rome when Julius Caesar was assassinated].
cards.real: Cleopatra ruled for about 21 years, from 51 BC until her death in 30 BC, when she was 39.

cards.say: Oxford University [got its first royal charter from King Henry VIII], [was teaching students before the Aztecs founded their capital city], [didn't let women earn degrees until after World War I], and [had a group of its scholars leave and start Cambridge University].
cards.real: Oxford's first royal charter came in 1248, from King Henry III. Henry VIII wasn't born until 1491.

cards.say: The Hubble Space Telescope [went up into space before the first website went online], [was already in orbit when Google was founded], [launched with a main mirror that was ground to the wrong shape], and [took the first photo ever of a black hole, in 2019].
cards.real: The first black hole photo, shown in 2019, came from the Event Horizon Telescope, a team of radio telescopes linked up around Earth.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Hubble launched on April 24, 1990; Google was founded in September 1998 https://asd.gsfc.nasa.gov/archive/hubble/missions/sm1.html

cards.say: The Great Pyramid of Giza [was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for more than 3,700 years], [took its builders about 90 years of work to finish], [was built while woolly mammoths were still alive], and [has graffiti inside left by the work crews who built it].
cards.real: Most estimates say it took about 20 to 27 years to build, for the pharaoh Khufu, around 2600 BC.

cards.say: Tutankhamun [ruled Egypt more than 1,000 years after the Great Pyramid was built], [had the first royal tomb ever found in the Valley of the Kings], [became pharaoh when he was only eight or nine years old], and [had his tomb found the same year the BBC started broadcasting].
cards.real: Royal tombs there were found long before his, like Seti I's in 1817. Tut's, found in 1922, was famous because it was nearly intact.

cards.say: The Colosseum [opened more than 100 years after Julius Caesar died], [had a giant sun awning worked by hundreds of sailors], [was already 1,000 years old when Oxford University started teaching], and [was opened by Emperor Nero with 100 days of games].
cards.real: Emperor Titus opened it in AD 80 with 100 days of games. Nero had died in AD 68, before work on it even began.

cards.say: Leif Erikson [grew up in Norway, the homeland of his Viking ancestors], [reached North America about 500 years before Columbus], [landed in America before William the Conqueror invaded England], and [was the son of the explorer who gave Greenland its name].
cards.real: Leif was probably born in Iceland and grew up in Greenland, where his father, Erik the Red, set up the first Viking settlement.

cards.say: Leonardo da Vinci [started painting the Mona Lisa after Columbus reached the Americas], [designed a robot knight more than 500 years ago], [was born while Joan of Arc was still alive in France], and [had his Mona Lisa stolen in 1911 and missing for over two years].
cards.real: Joan of Arc died in 1431. Leonardo was born in 1452, more than 20 years later.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Joan of Arc died on May 30, 1431; Leonardo da Vinci was born on April 15, 1452 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_da_Vinci

cards.say: Benjamin Franklin [was alive at the same time as Isaac Newton], [watched one of the first balloon flights to carry people, in Paris], [lived long enough to see George Washington become president], and [got rich from the patents on his inventions].
cards.real: Franklin never patented any of his inventions. He wrote that since we gain from the inventions of others, we should share ours freely.

cards.say: Orville Wright [made his famous first flight while Queen Victoria was still alive], [made his famous first flight while Harriet Tubman was still alive], [lived long enough to see a plane fly faster than sound], and [kept that famous first flight in the air for just 12 seconds].
cards.real: Queen Victoria died in January 1901, almost three years before Orville flew at Kitty Hawk on December 17, 1903.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Orville's first flight on December 17, 1903 lasted 12 seconds and covered 120 feet https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_Flyer

cards.say: Sputnik 1 [went into orbit before NASA had even been created], [was a metal ball only about 23 inches wide], [launched closer in time to the first airplane flight than to the first iPhone], and [went up less than 12 years before people walked on the Moon].
cards.real: Sputnik went up in October 1957, almost 54 years after the first airplane flight in 1903 but less than 50 years before the first iPhone in 2007.

cards.say: Apollo 11 [landed on the Moon before the first home video game console went on sale], [touched down while a Civil War veteran was still alive], [ended with its crew filling out a customs form back on Earth], and [landed less than 66 years after the Wright brothers' first flight].
cards.real: The last known Civil War veteran, Albert Woolson, died in 1956, 13 years before Apollo 11 landed in July 1969.
